chunks.arabic_text: إِرْشَادُ الْمُفِيدِ: ابْنُ قُولَوَيْهَ، عَنِ الْكُلَيْنِيِّ، عَنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى، عَنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى، عَن أَبِي يَحْيَى الْوَاسِطِيِّ، عَنِ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ قَالَ

translations.en: Al-Irshad of al-Mufid: Ibn Qulawayh, from al-Kulayni, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from Hisham ibn Salim who said:

chunks.arabic_text: كُنَّا بِالْمَدِينَةِ بَعْدَ وَفَاةِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام أَنَا وَمُحَمَّدُ بْنُ النُّعْمَانِ صَاحِبُ الطَّاقِ، وَالنَّاسُ مُجْتَمِعُونَ عِنْدَ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ أَنَّهُ صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ بَعْدَ أَبِيهِ، فَدَخَلْنَا عَلَيْهِ وَالنَّاسُ عِنْدَهُ فَسَأَلْنَاهُ عَنِ الزَّكَاةِ فِي كَمْ تَجِبُ؟ قَالَ: فِي مِائَتَيْ دِرْهَمٍ خَمْسَةُ دَرَاهِمَ، فَقُلْنَا: فَفِي مِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ؟ قَالَ: دِرْهَمَانِ وَنِصْفٌ، قُلْنَا: وَاللَّهُ مَا تَقُولُ الْمُرْجِئَةُ هَذَا فَقَالَ: وَاللَّهُ مَا أَدْرِي مَا تَقُولُ الْمُرْجِئَةُ، قَالَ: فَخَرَجْنَا ضَلَالاً … قُلْتُ: جَعَلْتُ فَدَاكَ إِنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ أَخَاكَ يَزْعُمُ أَنَّهُ الْإِمَامُ بَعْدَ أَبِيهِ فَقَالَ: عَبْدُ اللَّهِ يُرِيدُ أَنْ لَا يُعْبَدَ اللَّهُ … وَبَقِيَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ لَا يَدْخُلُ إِلَيْهِ مِنَ النَّاسِ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ

translations.en: We were in Medina after the death of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), myself and Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man (Sahib al-Taq), and the people were gathered around Abdallah ibn Ja'far, considering him to be the master of the affair after his father. We entered upon him while the people were with him, and we asked him about the Zakat: at what amount is it levied? He said: five dirhams for two hundred dirhams. We said: and for one hundred dirhams? He said: two and a half dirhams. We said: By Allah, this is what the Murji'ah say! He said: By Allah, I do not know what the Murji'ah say! He said: So we came out feeling lost... I said: May I be your ransom, your brother Abdallah claims that he is the Imam after his father. He said: Abdallah wants that Allah not be worshipped... And Abdallah remained such that not many people entered to see him except a few.

en.summary: This hadith from al-Mufid’s *Irshad* highlights the post-Sadiq succession dispute by contrasting Abdallah ibn Ja'far’s correct but superficial knowledge of Zakat with the narrator’s critique of his theological depth. The narrator’s remark that Abdallah 'wants not to worship God' suggests a perceived lack of *Ismah* or profound spiritual authority, leading to his eventual isolation. This narrative serves as a key Shia argument against the validity of the Salihiyyah claim, emphasizing that mere ritual correctness does not equate to Imamate.
en.seo_question: What evidence is presented in Shia sources regarding Abdallah ibn Ja'far's claim to Imamate after his father?
